issues.description: The problem statement's UML and the solution expect Stock.take(String) to return an int (returning -1 on failure or the remaining quantity on success), but the template implementation declares Stock.take(String) as returning boolean. This mismatch is structural and will confuse students (and break implementations) because the intended API (per the UML and solution) uses numeric return values to indicate remaining quantity or failure.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template's Stock.take method signature and implementation to return an int (not boolean). Make it return -1 when the ingredient is missing or out of stock, and otherwise decrement the quantity and return the remaining quantity — matching the UML in the problem statement and the solution implementation.

issues.description: The Stock.take method's contract differs between the problem statement (UML) and the template code vs. the reference solution. The UML in problem_statement.md defines Stock.take(String): int, the solution implements take(String) returning an int, but the template's Stock.take(String) returns a boolean. This mismatch of the method's return type for the same conceptual operation (taking one unit of an ingredient from stock) creates mapping confusion for students: they will see a different API in the starter code than what the exercise describes and what the solution uses.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the UML and solution by changing the template Stock.take(String) signature and implementation to return an int (e.g., returning the new quantity or -1 on failure). Alternatively, if boolean is intended, update the UML and the solution to use boolean consistently. Prefer making the template match the UML/solution to avoid student confusion.
